subject: How to create a plot with a broken y-axis in one of the panels in a multi-panel plot

messages.author: 28a384cf34cebfbc
messages.subject: How to create a plot with a broken y-axis in one of the panels in a multi-panel plot
parts:
Hi,

 

I am looking for help: does someone know how to draw a broken axis like shown in Figure 10.16 (page 186) in the book “lattice” by Deepayan Sarkar. However, that figure (Figure 10.16) is a single panel plot. What I need is a broken axis in one of the panels in a multi-panel plot. The code I used essentially as below:

 

library("lattice");

xyplot(currVal ~ currTime | currGene, curr0, type = c('p', 'a'),

       groups = currCond, key = key.variety3a, as.table = TRUE,

       pch = 1:2,

       col.line = c('blue', 'orange'), col.symbol = c('blue', 'orange'),

       layout = c(1, 6),

       scales = list(y = list(relation = 'free', at=list(c(0, 400000,800000, 1200000,1600000),

c(0,700000,1400000,2100000,2800000),pretty(c(0, 800000), n = 4),c(0, 15000,30000, 45000,60000),

c(0,80000,160000,240000,320000),c(0,150000,300000,450000,600000)), rot = 0, cex = 0.7)),

       strip = FALSE, strip.left = TRUE,

       xlab = "Time Course",

       ylab = "Normalized copy number/ng of Total RNA",

       main = "RT-PCR Time Course With Average")

 

This will plot a 6-panel time course plot for 6 different genes. But one of the panels (i.e., the last second) with y-axis ranged from 0 to 320000 (see the at parameter in scales()). I wish to split the y-axis into two ranges (just like the Figure 10.16), say, one from 0 to 200000, then the other from 300000 to 320000. Anybody has similar example or know how to do it?

 

Thanks a bunch!

 

Best,

 

Myi
